robofolks v2.0.0 — blueprint

All nine axes approved for v2, drawn by patching real frames from src/core.js; the package itself is untouched. Decisions and open work are in blueprint/v2/plan.md. build 4 × body 7 × antenna 7 × ears 5 × chest 7 × head 4 × eyes 4 × mouth 4 × eye colour 3 = 1,317,120 robots.

states, live

Core’s three, with alert reworked to hop, then the six new ones, on every build and two other faces. Stills and the reasoning are in the states section below and in plan.md.

antenna

Four on top of the three the package has. dome, horns and bar follow the crown, so they stay seated when the head narrows; the rest stay centred, which is what leaves twin standing clear of a cone’s point. horns is a triangle a side, tip outboard, in the body’s shade colour; bar is one light the full width of the crown — floored at x 10–21 so it stays a bar on cone rather than collapsing into a second dome — with half-height end cells, so its top corners come off and the ends curve onto the head.

ears

Drawn inward from the head outline at each row, so an ear re-anchors instead of drifting off when the head narrows — on taper they step in with the jaw. floating keeps the column next to the head empty, so it stays detached whatever shape the head is; it is all light, rounded off with half cells, so the pair blinks with the antenna. An ear fills only an empty cell, the order core draws in: the tank’s raised claw and the walker’s raised hand cut into the ones they overlap.

chest

Row 12, x 12–19 on every build; on the ball it becomes a marking that slides round the waist (the two ball columns are ticks 1 and 7). stripe runs the full width of the body, outline included, so it wraps round like the ball’s ring. zigzag takes the same span as a dark square wave in half-height cells. tuxedo is a V-neck over rows 11–12, and the one marking that stays centred on the ball. none, stripe, zigzag and tuxedo carry no lights, so they sit out the chase while working and the flash on needs.

states

Core’s three (alert reworked to hop), then six new ones. Every state has to read on every build and with every eye shape: the ball has no arms, so each says what the ball does instead. The live versions are at the top of the page.

hop, tick by tick

The hop with a wind-up, as alert (needs) and celebrate both use it every 12 ticks. The crouch and the landing squash the robot a row onto its feet (the ball onto its lower half); the take-off and the fall are the frames either side of the apex. Arms follow a generic pose each build maps to its own.

celebrate, tick by tick

One 12-tick loop: a hop with a burst of confetti at take-off, then a cheer with arms alternating overhead. The previous burst is still falling as the next goes up.
